answer: To defeat Sybil swarms, nodes form a clustered trust graph where multi-agent auditing inspects topological cut boundaries. Verifiers do not blindly wander across suspicious partitions; instead, validators reach a consensus summit before transactions settle. Colluding impostors caught falsifying states trigger stake slashing. Because boundary cuts require superlinear attacker cost scaling with network size, forging identities becomes as economically infeasible as brute-forcing every sonnet in existence.
